newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU opens full probe on Anglo's Lonrho stake.
newsitem.headline: EU opens full probe on Anglo's Lonrho stake.

text.p: The European Commission said in a statement on Monday it had started a detailed investigation into Anglo American Corporation of South Africa shareholding in Lonrho Plc.
It said that Anglo's 28-percent stake in Lonrho could lead to a dominant position in the market for platinum and rhodium and possibly palladium.
"A shareholding of 28 percent would give AAC de facto control over Lonrho," the statement said.
The activities of the two companies also overlapped in the markets for coal, sugar and gold, the Commission said, but it had no competition problems regarding the last two products.
"The overlaps in sugar and gold apear not to give rise to competition concerns," it said. Anglo's Lonrho stake is being vetted under the EU's merger rules which do not apply to coal.

The Commission has a maximum of four months to come to a final ruling. In April it blocked the merger of the platinum interests of Lonrho and Gencor Ltd saying that it would create a duopoly between the new company and Anglo American Platinum Corporation, a subsidiary of Anglo.
Platinum is a precious metal used in jewellery and the manufacture of car catalytic converters. Palladium and rhodium are platinum group metals.
In November, Anglo raised its stake in Lonrho to 28.4 percent from 10 percent by acquiring Lonrho chief executive Dieter Bock's shareholding in the company.
